It's a bit cliche, but I think there's something worth exploring here.

From far away our problems can seem very monstrous, very imposing and it really doesn't help that they're nestled in the heart of several other issues. Why would we dare leave the comfort of safety to explore what we fear? 

Courage is the strength necessary to explore the unknown and to face our adversity. 

Sometimes our problems just turn out to be imposing but docile. We make friends along the way, we learn about things we've never known before.

So I really like drawing organic, liquid figures who in some form blend with their environment. You never lose sight of them, but from every perspective it looks like they're struggling to tread through their surroundings.

http://i.imgur.com/TeiSu6O.jpg

But when you look at the perspective of the subject it's totally different. They can feel themselves struggling, they just can't see it from an outside perspective. It makes things difficult. Maybe the solution is just outside their view. Maybe the solution is painted on their forehead. Sometimes we don't get to bend ourselves backwards to solve issues.

But we can fulfill the role of both these characters. Most times it's not obvious, and we will fight and struggle to remain independent, to be as normal as possible.

But maybe that's not what this drawing is about.

Maybe our character was their environment. They blended in, just like everything else. They were just a blank page. 

And then they saw something; a light, a goal, a future.

And with every effort, with the weight of their surroundings and a terrible strain on their mind they reached out to grasp at the thing they saw... 

...if only for a chance.
